papers.title_en: Reducing Asymmetric Path TSP to Asymmetric TSP
papers.evidence: 将非对称路径TSP归约为非对称TSP，保持近似比
papers.tldr: 非对称路径TSP要求从指定起点到终点遍历所有点，其近似算法长期弱于非对称TSP。本文给出从非对称TSP到路径版本的归约：对任意常数α≥1与ε>0，把α近似算法转化为(α+ε)近似算法。此前Feige–Singh归约仅得α(2+ε)近似，新结果回答Traub–Vygen开放问题。由此非对称TSP的常数因子近似保证可几乎无损地移植到路径版本。
papers.abstract_en: In the Asymmetric Traveling Salesman Problem (Asymmetric TSP), we are given distances between $n$ vertices that satisfy the triangle inequality but need not be symmetric, and we seek a shortest tour through all vertices. In its path version, Asymmetric Path TSP, two vertices $s$ and $t$ are prescribed, and we seek a shortest path from $s$ to $t$ through all vertices. Both problems are equivalent to their versions with arbitrary nonnegative edge costs on a directed graph, in which vertices may be visited more than once. We show that for all constants $α\ge1$ and $\varepsilon>0$, any $α$-approximation algorithm for Asymmetric TSP yields an $(α+\varepsilon)$-approximation algorithm for Asymmetric Path TSP. The best previous reduction of this kind, due to Feige and Singh, yields an $α(2+\varepsilon)$-approximation algorithm. Our result answers an open question of Traub and Vygen. Consequently, every constant-factor approximation guarantee for Asymmetric TSP carries over to Asymmetric Path TSP up to an arbitrarily small additive error.

papers.title_en: Approximation Algorithms for Asymmetric Multi-Path TSP
papers.evidence: 非对称多路径TSP的近似算法，推广了ATSP
papers.tldr: 非对称多路径旅行商问题要求用k条分别指定起点与终点的游走覆盖全部顶点，并最小化所有游走总长度；一般情形下，多项式时间近似属于NP难。作者构造覆盖游走，在n^{O(k)}时间给出O(k)近似，回答Friggstad于2013年提出的开放问题。当所有起点相同且所有终点相同时，获多项式时间O(k)近似与双准则近似；多仓库情形获常数因子近似。该工作还改进了非对称后悔有界车辆路径与单位权重Path ATSP的近似算法。
papers.abstract_en: Asymmetric Multi-Path TSP is the generalization of the Asymmetric Traveling Salesperson Problem where we are looking for $k$ walks, each with prescribed start $s_i$ and prescribed end $t_i$, such that every vertex is visited by at least one of the walks. The objective is to minimize the total length of all walks. In general, it is NP-hard to find any approximation for this problem in polynomial time (even if the approximation factor is allowed to depend on the number of vertices). We show that one can obtain an $O(k)$-approximation in time $n^{O(k)}$, answering an open question by Friggstad [2013].   For the special case where all tour start vertices $s_i$ are identical and all end vertices $t_i$ are identical, we obtain an $O(k)$-approximation in polynomial time, as well as an $(O(\frac{1}ε), 1+ε)$-bicriteria approximation. For the multi-depot setting, where $s_i =t_i$ for all $i$, we obtain a constant-factor approximation in polynomial time.   Finally, our results imply improved constant-factor approximation algorithms for Asymmetric Regret-Bounded Vehicle Routing and unit-weight Path ATSP.

papers.title_en: Improved Approximation Algorithms for Multi-Path TSP and Ordered TSP
papers.evidence: 基于LP松弛取整的TSP变体近似算法
papers.tldr: 多路径TSP与有序TSP要求在一般度量下用路径或环游覆盖指定顶点，此前近似比分别约2.213和1.868。作者从LP解中为每对端点采样树并只保留端点间路径，证明连接全部顶点到这些路径的最便宜森林期望权重可由端点根森林与丢弃分支加权控制。多路径TSP结合多仓库原始-对偶增长权重，得到确定性1.8833近似并约束积分间隙；有序TSP得到1.7910近似。该统一框架同时改进两类问题的近似比与积分间隙。
papers.abstract_en: In Multi-Path TSP, given a metric and $k$ pairs of vertices $(s_i,t_i)$, where $k$ is part of the input, we seek $s_i$--$t_i$ paths of minimum total length that together visit all vertices. Ratios below $2$ were known only for graphic metrics and special cases such as multiple depots ($s_i=t_i$); in general metrics, the best ratio was $1+2e^{-1/2}\approx2.213$, by a randomized algorithm of Böhm, Friggstad, Mömke and Spoerhase [SODA 2025]. We give a deterministic algorithm with ratio $\frac{5e-2}{3e-2}<1.8833$ relative to a restriction of their LP relaxation, bounding its integrality gap by the same constant. For Ordered TSP, where a tour must visit $k$ given vertices in a prescribed cyclic order, we compute tours within $1+\frac{e}{2(e-1)}<1.7910$ times the value of the LP relaxation of Armbruster, Mnich and Nägele [APPROX 2024], improving $\frac32+\frac1e\approx1.868$ on both the ratio and the integrality gap. Our algorithms sample a tree for every pair (for Ordered TSP, every two consecutive given vertices) from an LP solution, but keep only the path between the two endpoints. Our main lemma shows that, for arbitrary nonnegative edge weights, a cheapest forest connecting all vertices to these paths has expected weight at most $1/e$ times that of a cheapest forest rooted at the endpoints plus $(1-1/e)$ times the expected weight of the discarded branches. For Multi-Path TSP, we use the weights of a primal--dual growth process that Zhao, Liu and Xiao [arXiv 2026] designed for multiple depots; in these weights, the connecting forest also pays for part of correcting its degree parities.
